live_production_database_verification.note: Run against production project bwrnnmzqipnoakmdbevz. Every probe touching public.forms ran inside a transaction that was ROLLED BACK, because that table carries the AFTER INSERT trigger forms_to_google_sheets. THE ROLLBACK CLAIM WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED - 'a rollback undoes an HTTP request' is false in general, and says nothing whatsoever about Resend emails, which are sent over HTTP from the application and are irreversible. What was checked is narrower and specific to this trigger: supabase_functions.http_request is plpgsql and calls net.http_post; pg_net is version 0.14.0, which implements net.http_post as an INSERT into net.http_request_queue in the CALLER'S transaction; probed directly, the queue held 1 row inside the transaction and 0 after rollback, with no row recorded in net._http_response; and the background worker runs in a separate backend, so MVCC prevents it from ever seeing an uncommitted queue row. This conclusion does not generalise to other side effects, and should be re-verified if pg_net is upgraded.

Own ticket; not changed here.

page_validation_fail_closed.change: Removed the empty-value escape hatch. META_LEAD_PAGE_IDS may only ADD pages; the handoff Page is compiled in and cannot be removed. A missing page id is rejected, and no configuration makes an arbitrary page authorized.
page_validation_fail_closed.why: A present-but-empty env var is trivially produced by a bad copy-paste or a templating tool that emits empty strings for unset values, so the control could be disabled by accident with no signal.

restricted_quarantine.change: An unauthorized form OR Page now gets sendMetaQuarantineAlert - form id, page id, lead id and reason only, with a deliberately distinguishable subject - instead of the full scheduling email. The lead is still STORED, so nothing is lost and an authorized operator can recover it.
restricted_quarantine.why: Routing an unverifiable lead into the scheduling inbox let a stray leadgen subscription, or an attacker on an unrelated Page, put arbitrary contact details in front of staff in a message indistinguishable from a real patient request. Staff would then call a stranger or a planted number.
restricted_quarantine.single_alert_guarantee: Both alert kinds claim the same staff-notification delivery key, so exactly one is ever sent per lead and a misconfiguration cannot flood the inbox.
restricted_quarantine.patient_email: A quarantined lead never claims a patient-confirmation send, so no provider call is possible even with the flag on.

anon_impersonation_blocked.change: The public.forms insert policy no longer uses with check (true). anon/authenticated may not set external_lead_id, external_form_id, external_form_version or external_submitted_at, and may not claim form_source=meta-instant-form.
abuses_closed: forging form_source=meta-instant-form to fake channel attribution and cost-per-lead
RESERVING an external_lead_id so the real webhook insert is refused as a duplicate and the stored row is the attacker's
anon_impersonation_blocked.could_it_ever_trigger_an_email: No, before or after. Outbound mail is created only on the signature-verified webhook path; nothing reads public.forms to decide what to send - no poller, no trigger-driven mailer, no row-watcher. This was always a data-integrity hole, not an email hole.
anon_impersonation_blocked.website_compatibility: PRESERVED - verified in production that a normal anon website insert still succeeds, and that 0 of 1,400 existing rows carry any external_* value.

privileged_meta_ingestion.change: logLeadToSupabase selects the client by whether an external_lead_id is present. Website submissions keep the publishable key and their existing trust model untouched; Meta ingestion writes as service_role.
why: Required by the tightened policy above, which deliberately forbids anon from writing external_*.
createClient() reads cookies(), and this path runs inside waitUntil after the response, where there is no meaningful cookie scope and no browser to act for.
privileged_meta_ingestion.failure_mode: A missing SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY fails loudly rather than producing an RLS violation that reads like schema drift. Staff alerts still send, and the ingestion queue keeps the lead recoverable.

waituntil_durability.change: The leadgen id is recorded SYNCHRONOUSLY in public.meta_lead_ingestions before the webhook returns 200. A failed Graph lookup or insert records a sanitized code and stays retryable; the 30-minute cron re-drives up to 10 pending leads per run; retries are bounded at 5, then the row waits for a human.
waituntil_durability.why: Everything after the 200 ran in one in-memory waitUntil promise. A dead invocation or a failed Graph lookup meant the lead was gone - Meta already had its 200 and would never retry, and nothing in the database knew the lead had existed.
waituntil_durability.safe_to_redrive: Every step is keyed on a unique column - ingestion on leadgen_id, the lead row on external_lead_id, each message on delivery_key - so a retry resumes rather than duplicates.
waituntil_durability.asymmetry: Lead ingestion IS re-driven; message delivery is NOT. A message stuck in processing may or may not have reached the provider and that is unknowable from here, so it is flagged unknown for a human. Re-driving ingestion risks nothing; resending an email on a guess puts a duplicate in a patient's inbox.
waituntil_durability.code_location: lib/meta-lead-ingest.ts - moved out of the route because an App Router route module may export only route handlers (an extra export is a hard type error) and the cron needs the same code.

apps_script_lead_sheet.duplicates: Now prevented UPSTREAM, which is the effective fix: the trigger is AFTER INSERT, and the unique forms_external_lead_id_key means a Meta retry no longer produces a second insert, so no second POST. Before this work a retry produced a duplicate sheet line.
apps_script_lead_sheet.failures: Silent, and unchanged. net.http_post is fire-and-forget with a 5000ms timeout and nothing inspects net._http_response, so if Apps Script is down the row is in Supabase and never reaches the sheet, with no alert. The lead is not lost - Supabase is the system of record - but the sheet silently diverges. Worth its own ticket; out of scope here.
apps_script_lead_sheet.forged_rows: A generic forged website lead can still add a fake sheet line. The Meta-shaped version of that is now blocked. Pre-existing.

meta_token_rotation.status: PLAN CONFIRMED FEASIBLE - NOTHING ROTATED OR REVOKED
meta_token_rotation.verified: System User token on app MSO Marketing API (1857329048632570), System User 122096384031489946, scopes include leads_retrieval, issued 2026-09-22, neverExpires: true - so it will not roll over on its own and rotation has to be deliberate.
meta_token_rotation.feasibility: Generating a new System User token does not invalidate existing ones, so the test-before-revoke ordering is achievable.
meta_token_rotation.caveat: If the cleanest way to invalidate one specific System User token is resetting the APP SECRET, that is the same secret verifying X-Hub-Signature-256 on this webhook. Resetting it would break signature verification until META_APP_SECRET is updated and redeployed, and would invalidate every other token on that app including the Meta API environment's. env_var_scope.finding: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY was saved to Production, Preview AND Development. Only Production was needed.
env_var_scope.why_it_matters: There is one Supabase project behind every environment (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL is scoped to All Environments), so a Preview deployment can now bypass RLS on the LIVE patient database holding 1,400 records. The Development scope means `vercel env pull` writes the key into a local .env on any developer machine.
env_var_scope.severity: Moderate. Previews are behind Deployment Protection so not publicly reachable, and no preview receives Meta webhooks (Meta posts only to the production URL). But it widens access to patient data for no benefit, which is the opposite of the access-minimisation in docs/healthcare-privacy-remediation.md.
env_var_scope.action: Delete the Preview and Development rows for SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY; keep Production. CRON_SECRET on all three is harmless (Vercel Cron only runs in production) and can be left.

deployment_reliability_finding.cause: next/font/google downloads font CSS at build time. The redeploy ran with 'Skipping build cache, deployment was triggered without cache', so it had to re-fetch from Google Fonts and hit a transient failure.

deployment_reliability_finding.why_it_is_worth_recording: A cache-less production build of this repo can fail on a Google Fonts hiccup. That is a deploy-reliability risk precisely when it would hurt most: an emergency rollback or redeploy. Mitigation if it recurs: retry the build, or self-host the font via next/font/local. Out of scope here; no change made.
